name: Brachydactyly-preaxial Hallux Varus Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Brachydactyly-preaxial Hallux Varus Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of preaxial hallux varus deformity (medial deviation of the great toe)
Shortening of the digits (brachydactyly) affecting fingers and toes
Radiographic evidence of shortened phalanges and metatarsals consistent with brachydactyly
Positive family history of similar limb anomalies
No evidence of other syndromic malformations or systemic involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of preaxial hallux varus deformity and brachydactyly confirmed clinically and radiographically
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by radiographic findings; genetic testing may assist but is not definitive.

imaging: Radiographs showing shortened phalanges and metatarsals
X-ray evidence of medial deviation of the great toe
genetic: Possible mutations in genes related to limb development (e.g., HOXD13), though no definitive genetic marker established
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic toe deformities

distinguishingFeatures: Isolated shortening of the distal phalanx of the thumb
More severe limb malformations including absence of digits

redFlags: Progressive worsening of foot deformity causing severe functional impairment
Presence of systemic abnormalities suggesting syndromic association
Severe pain or signs of infection in affected foot
references: Orphanet: Brachydactyly-preaxial Hallux Varus Syndrome - ORPHA:1278
Fryns JP, et al. Brachydactyly with preaxial hallux varus: a distinct entity. Clin Dysmorphol. 1990.
